question: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are extremely difficult to break down and can accumulate in soil, water, plants, animals and humans. Certain PFAS can damage the immune and reproductive systems and cause cancer. Materials containing PFAS in wind turbines can release these substances into the environment.

In its answer to parliamentary question E002887/20261, the Commission does not dispute the potential risks. It states that the European Chemicals Agency has been assessing a proposal to restrict all PFAS since 2023. Wind turbines are explicitly included among the uses of PFAS covered.
The Commission added: ‘While waiting for ECHA’s final scientific assessment, the Commission cannot anticipate how the use of PFAS in wind turbines will be addressed.’ 1.

How will the Commission ensure that the precautionary principle is upheld during the further expansion of wind power, until such time as the potential environmental and health risks posed by materials containing PFAS in wind turbines have not been conclusively assessed scientifically?

When will the Commission decide, on the basis of the ECHA’s assessment, on possible restrictions on PFAS in wind turbines, and what measures are planned to prevent potential damage to the environment and human health or to protect those already affected?
